episodes.title: 78% Wanted This AI Feature. Almost Nobody Used It - Supriya Subudhi, Bumble
episodes.description:
Bumble product manager Supriya Subudhi shares five lessons from A/B testing an AI photo feedback feature in a dating app with over 20 million monthly users. 78% of surveyed users said they wanted feedback, but only 10-15% used it; the average win hid odd outputs like telling smiling people to smile more; the best model cost about 10x more; switching to a cheaper model also shrank the results; and regulation meant the feature couldn't ship outside the US. She closes with five questions to ask before you call any AI test a win.

episodes.title: When Running Your Own AI Models Beats Paying for APIs - Steven Latré, imec
episodes.description:
Steven Latré leads AI at imec, the Belgian semiconductor R&D center, and his team ran thousands of benchmark runs to find out what moving from APIs to your own GPUs really costs for long-running coding agents. Testing open-weight models and three coding harnesses on SWE-Bench Pro, they found that hardware costs jump in steps rather than a smooth curve, that concurrency matters even more than accuracy, that break-even GPU utilization ranges from 89% on small systems to about 15% on 8x B200 machines, and that the right harness can cut GPU time in half for the same result.

episodes.title: Voice AI Where One Wrong Question Breaks the Rules - Shiv Indap, Upstart & Brooke Hopkins, Coval
episodes.description:
Upstart handles thousands of lending calls a day, where one wrong question can become a regulatory problem. Shiv Indap, who leads voice AI at Upstart, and Brooke Hopkins, founder of Coval and former head of evaluation infrastructure at Waymo, walk through automating loan verification calls: the compliance traps, outgrowing a Google Sheet for human review, and raising agreement between the LLM judge and human reviewers from 33% to 92%. Then they lay out the full loop from live monitoring and human review queues to re-simulating fixes and self-healing agents, with every change still signed off by a human.

episodes.title: How to Decide What Your AI Agent Should Remember - Wojciech Pluta, Oracle
episodes.description:
RAG gives agents a way to read, but memory gives them a way to write, and that's where your business value lives. Wojciech Pluta, head of technical marketing for Oracle AI Database, explains memory promotion: deciding what's worth keeping, checking it against existing records and admitting, rejecting or escalating it to a human. A mortgage-agent demo remembers an operator's preferences across sessions and refuses to store an "approve every application" rule. He also covers short-term, long-term and shared memory, why to store memory in a database, and the context card that keeps prompts lean.

episodes.title: Your AI Agent Starts Every Session Like a New Hire - Killian Carlsen-Phelan, Sonar
episodes.description:
Every new coding agent session starts like a new hire: it doesn't know your conventions, architecture rules or approved libraries, so it burns time and tokens searching your repo and repeats the issues already in it. Killian Carlsen-Phelan of Sonar introduces Sonar Vortex, a plugin that hands your agent a map of the codebase and your guidelines before it writes, then deterministically checks every edit. In a live session, Vortex catches a temp-file permission bug the agent's own tests missed, and rejects its first fix. Sonar reports 36% fewer tokens and 44% fewer production outages.

episodes.title: Your Agent Just Paid for Nothing: 6 Attacks on x402 Payments - Ishween Kaur, SoFi
episodes.description:
x402 lets AI agents pay for data and APIs with tiny on-chain payments over HTTP. Ishween Kaur explains how the protocol works, then walks through six of the 20 ways she broke it in a safe test environment: price changes in the payment header, paying twice, getting data for free, one payment unlocking many pages, lookalike sellers, and prompt injection that talks an agent into paying again. For each one, she shows the guard that stopped it and how to roll out agent payments safely, trace by trace.

episodes.title: Why AI Won't Replace Stock Pickers - Jack Woodruff, Candlestick & Vinoo Ganesh, Kepler
episodes.description:
Jack Woodruff, founder and former CIO of long/short equity fund Candlestick Capital and a former Citadel portfolio manager, sits down with Kepler CEO Vinoo Ganesh to talk about what AI really changes in fundamental investing. They discuss why humans are still the bottleneck, how AI turns hours of prep into minutes and raises the table stakes, why you should never trust a number you can't audit, where edge comes from when every fund has the same models, how fund teams will be structured, and why the "no-analyst hedge fund" won't beat the best human-led funds.

episodes.title: The Cheaper AI Model That Costs You More - Rayan Krishnan, Vals AI
episodes.description:
Vals AI builds benchmarks that frontier labs cite in their model cards, and Rayan Krishnan explains why those single scores hide a jagged frontier. In finance tasks like tax and Excel LBO modeling, the best model changes by task, and a model that's cheaper on paper can cost more and score lower because it burns extra tokens. He shares lessons from building benchmarks (the right accuracy metric, reward hacking, multi-turn work), a case study of a team that spent $1.5M on tokens in a month before cutting spend about 90% with internal evals, and why a firm's own work history is its best eval.

episodes.title: Catch the Bugs Your Code Review Misses - Killian Carlsen-Phelan & Taylor Luttrell-Williams, Sonar
episodes.description:
In this hands-on session, Killian Carlsen-Phelan and Taylor Luttrell-Williams of Sonar set up Gitar, a code change verification agent, on a sample ticketing app and run three pull requests through it. Gitar catches a bug that isn't in the diff at all (a buyer can refund a ticket after giving it to a friend), enforces a business rule from a project config (show customers the all-in price), then diagnoses a failing CI test and keeps pushing fixes until the PR passes and auto-merges. They close with functional validation against Jira tickets, learned conventions, and cross-repo and cross-PR analysis.

episodes.title: Why Humans Can't Keep Up With AI-Written Code - Tariq Shaukat, Sonar
episodes.description:
Agents have made code cheap: one study saw lines of code up 2,450% but releases up only 30%. Sonar CEO Tariq Shaukat draws on the factory revolution that Toyota and Lexus started to explain how to build agentic software factories you can trust. He breaks down five hard problems: human review that doesn't scale (people agree with AI that's wrong 4 out of 5 times), agents struggling with large codebases, errors compounding over long tasks, unreliable LLM judges, and near-zero time to exploit. Then he lays out Sonar's code confidence formula: intent, guide rails, verification and evidence.
